key_insight: Physics-informed neural networks identify plate orientations for near-isotropic, ultrastiff lattices, with six plates found to be the minimum required.
engineering_relevance: These architectures offer a systematic route to lightweight structures with high specific stiffness and nearly direction-independent elastic response.
method: Apply PINNs to analytical equations to solve for plate orientations.
Assemble orientations into closed-cell, quasi-random foam geometries and evaluate them using finite element simulations.
Additively manufacture six-plate geometries using LAPIS and characterize them experimentally.
evidence_signal: Reported lattices reach 90% of the Hashin–Shtrikman stiffness upper bound at relative density 0.4 and a near-isotropic Zener ratio of 0.95 at relative density 0.1.
watch_item: Suboptimal plate placement introduces bending, so orientation solutions alone do not guarantee realization of the theoretical stiffness limit.
paper_title: Derivation of Novel Isotropic Metamaterials at the Hashin Shtrikman Stiffness Limit Enabled by Physics Informed Neural Networks
